{{verse|chapter=15|verse=21}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Thur{{ls}}day the fifth weeke in Lent.}}And {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent forth from thence and retired into the quarters of Tyre and Sidon. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=22}}† And behold {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 7, 25.''}}* a vvoman of Chanaan came forth out of tho{{ls}}e coa{{ls}}tes, and crying out, {{ls}}ayd to him, Haue mercie vpon me, O lord the Sonne of Dauid: my daughter is {{ls}}ore vexed of a Deuil. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=23}}† VVho an{{ls}}vvered her not a word. And his Di{{ls}}ciples came and be{{ls}}ought him {{ls}}aying, Dimi{{ls}}se her: becau{{ls}}e {{ls}}he crieth out after vs: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=24}}† And he an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid: I was not {{ls}}ent but to the {{ls}}heepe that are lo{{ls}}t of the hou{{ls}}e of I{{ls}}rael. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=25}}† But {{ls}}he came and adored him, {{ls}}aying, Lord, help me. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=26}}† Who an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid: It is not good to take the bread of the Children, and to ca{{ls}}t it to the dogges. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=27}}† But {{ls}}he {{ls}}aid, Yea lord: for the vvhelpes al{{ls}}o eate of the crummes that fal from the table of their mai{{ls}}ters. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=28}}† Then {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvering {{ls}}aid to her, O vvoman, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ It were a {{ls}}traunge ca{{ls}}e that Chri{{ls}}t {{ls}}hould commend in this woman a {{ls}}ole faith without good workes, that is to {{ls}}ay, a dead faith {{ls}}uch as could not worke by loue, and which S. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=29}}† And when {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas pa{{ls}}{{ls}}ed from thence, he came be{{ls}}ide the {{ls}}ea of Galilee: and a{{ls}}cending into the mountaine, {{ls}}ate there. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=30}}† And there came to him great multitudes, hauing with them dumme per{{ls}}ons, blinde, lame, feeble, and many others: and they ca{{ls}}t them dovvne at his feete, and he cured them: {{verse|chapter=15|verse=31}}† {{ls}}o that the multitudes marueled {{ls}}eeing the dumme {{ls}}peake, the lame vvalke, the blinde {{ls}}ee: and they magnified the God of I{{ls}}rael. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=32}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 8, 1.''}}* {{sc|Iesvs}} called together his Di{{ls}}ciples, and {{ls}}aid: I pitie the multitude: becau{{ls}}e three dayes novv they continue vvith me, and haue not vvhat to eate: and dimi{{ls}}se them fa{{ls}}ting I vvil not, le{{ls}}t they fainte in the vvay. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=33}}† And the di{{ls}}ciples {{ls}}ay vnto him: vvhence then may vve gette {{ls}}o many loaues in the de{{ls}}ert as to fil {{ls}}o great a multitude? {{verse|chapter=15|verse=34}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}ayd to them, Hovv many loaues haue you? but they {{ls}}ayd, Seuen, & a fevv litle fi{{ls}}hes. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=35}}† And he commaunded the multitude to {{ls}}it dovvne vpon the ground. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=36}}† And taking the {{ls}}euen loaues & the fi{{ls}}hes, and geuing thankes, he brake, & gaue to his di{{ls}}ciples, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here we {{ls}}ee againe that the people mu{{ls}}t not be their owne caruers, nor receiue the Sacraments or other {{ls}}piritual {{ls}}u{{ls}}tenance immediatly of Chri{{ls}}t, or at their owne hād, but of their {{ls}}piritual gouerners.}}∷ the di{{ls}}ciples gaue to the people. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=37}}† And they did al eate, and had their fill. And that vvhich vvas left of the fragments they tooke vp, {{ls}}euen ba{{ls}}kets ful. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=38}}† And there vvere that did eate, foure thou{{ls}}and men, be{{ls}}ide children & women. {{verse|chapter=15|verse=39}}† And hauing dimi{{ls}}sed the multitude, he vvent vp into a boate, and came into the coa{{ls}}tes of Magedan.<noinclude>{{rh|||ANNO-}}</noinclude>
